claim: Ni (1996-Jun 2005, flagged: sample ends before 2015): average return to buying one-month single-stock calls (no ex-dividend date before expiry) at bid-ask midpoint and holding to expiry, unhedged, no trading costs beyond midpoint, was 2.31%, 2.50%, 1.98%, -10.15%, -36.86% for strike/stock <=0.85, 0.85-0.95, 0.95-1.05, 1.05-1.15, >1.15. Figures read on a secondary page reproducing pp. 42-46 of the paper, not the paper itself.
quote: Average one-month return of holding call option to expiration using bid-ask-midpoint prices (%)

claim: Bali, Beckmeyer, Moerke, Weigert (sample 1996-2020, >12m observations): the return studied is the monthly DELTA-HEDGED option return, not the outright buyer's return; average monthly delta-hedged return is -0.01% (median -0.34%); buckets are short (<=90 days) vs long (>90 days) maturity and ITM/ATM/OTM. No costs in the headline average. Not usable as buyer return.
quote: Panel A of Table 1 shows that the average monthly delta-hedged option return is −0.01%, whereas the median monthly delta-hedged option return is −0.34%.
title: Option Return Predictability with Machine Learning and Big Data (CFR WP 21-08, Aug 2021)

claim: Christoffersen, Goyenko, Jacobs, Karoui (sample Jan 1996 to Dec 2007, 341 firms, flagged pre-2015): average relative quoted bid-ask spread of short-term (20-70 days to maturity) OTM calls is 34.02% and of long-term (71-180 days) OTM calls is 22.67%; OTM most illiquid, then ATM, then ITM.
quote: the average relative spread of short-term OTM call options is 34.02%, while for long-term OTM calls the average spread is 22.67%.
title: Illiquidity Premia in the Equity Options Market (CREATES WP 2013-48)

claim: Muravyev and Pearson (2015 working paper; sample April 2003 to October 2006, flagged pre-2015; liquid equity options, no maturity or strike breakdown in the lines read): quoted spreads average 8.1 cents per share, conventional effective spreads 6.2 cents, average option price $1.70, stock spreads 1.4 cents.
quote: Conventionally measured effective spreads, which reflect the fact that trades tend to occur when quoted spreads are narrow, average 6.2 cents per share. For comparison, the average option price in our sample is $1.70.
url: https://c.mql5.com/forextsd/forum/209/Option Trading Costs Are Lower than You Think.pdf
title: Option Trading Costs Are Lower than You Think (working paper copy, 15 Mar 2015)

claim: Muravyev and Pearson: for the average trade, effective spreads adjusted for execution timing are one-third smaller than conventional effective spreads (April 2003-Oct 2006); the timing skill belongs to fast traders who trade just before option quotes move, so it does not describe an ordinary trader.
quote: For the average trade, effective spreads that take account of trade timing ability are one-third smaller than the conventionally measured effective spreads
url: https://c.mql5.com/forextsd/forum/209/Option Trading Costs Are Lower than You Think.pdf
title: Option Trading Costs Are Lower than You Think (working paper copy, 15 Mar 2015)

claim: Bryzgalova, Pavlova, Sikorskaya (Journal of Finance 2023; sample 4 Nov 2019 to 30 Jun 2021): retail investors prefer cheaper weekly options with average bid-ask spread of 12.6% and lose money on average (trading costs are the bulk of losses, measured from trade price to midquote).
quote: Retail investors prefer cheaper, weekly options with average bid-ask spread of 12.6%, and lose money on average.
url: https://lbsresearch.london.edu/id/eprint/2827/1/The Journal of Finance - 2023 - BRYZGALOVA - Retail Trading in Options and the Rise of the Big Three Wholesalers.pdf
title: Retail Trading in Options and the Rise of the Big Three Wholesalers

claim: Bryzgalova et al. (Nov 2019-Jun 2021): assuming a 10-day holding horizon the aggregate retail options portfolio lost $2.1 billion; aggregate retail trades lose money at all horizons tested; the bulk of the loss is indirect trading cost. quote: The bulk of the losses comes from the indirect costs of trading.
